annotationRationale: The main route relates quadratic coefficients to integer roots and exhausts the signed factor pairs. Factors and multiples support that enumeration. The quadratic formula, discriminant, and difference of squares are specific to the alternative route.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Algebra is appropriate; no area repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: The roots must have product 36. The four unequal positive factor pairs and their negatives give exactly eight distinct coefficient values, agreeing with choice B. The stem, choices and key are consistent; no figures or grading exceptions are supplied.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: 2022_AMC_10B_Q07/integer-root-pairs and 2022_AMC_10B_Q07/square-discriminant were both retained and independently verified against this identical question. AoPS Solution 4 is an equivalent factor-pair count. Its Pythagorean-triple route uses the same discriminant equation and would still need an exhaustive argument, so another method is unnecessary.
review.annotationCheck: Assessing cnm_226 and integer Diophantine equations, with factors and multiples as support, matches the main derivation. Quadratic-formula, discriminant and difference-of-squares nodes appropriately belong to the alternative route.
review.areaCheck: Algebra is appropriate; no area repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Expanding the factorization correctly gives rs=36 and k=−(r+s). Ordering positive roots bounds the smaller divisor below 6, yielding exactly (1,36), (2,18), (3,12), (4,9). Their negatives exhaust the negative-root case. The resulting values k=±37, ±20, ±15, ±13 are distinct, and equal-root pairs are excluded.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Correctly reuses 2022_AMC_10B_Q07#integer-root-pairs. Both inherited reference IDs, live-reference-2022_AMC_10B_Q07 and aops-reference-2022_AMC_10B_Q07, are retained. The current-question references corroborate the route. Project-method reuse is credited, and source-informed-original correctly distinguishes the explanation from official MAA material.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The opening explains why fixing the product helps. The factorization, bound on the smaller root, sign cases and explicit coefficient values make completeness and absence of duplicate counts reconstructible.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_226 precisely captures the roots-coefficients relationship, while math:integer-diophantine-equations captures the exhaustive integer restriction. Both are directly used.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The accepted exact cnm_226 link matches the roots-coefficients step. Supporting cnm_p153 matches enumeration of the factors of 36. The integer-solution synthesis has no supplied CN link.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: Neither immediate node has an accepted US link. Supporting cnm_p153 overlaps the factor-pair component of 4.OA.B.4; this does not establish its prime/composite requirements or a national alignment for the integer-root synthesis.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: The two immediate nodes are precise and sufficient. Question-level assessed and support roles correctly distinguish the main reasoning from elementary factor enumeration.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Integer roots force integer k and a positive integer root difference m with k²−m²=144. The parity argument correctly proves the converse. For k>0, the positive even factor pairs are exactly (2,72), (4,36), (6,24), (8,18), giving k=37,20,15,13. The equal pair gives repeated roots, k=0 is impossible, and negation supplies exactly four further values.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Correctly reuses 2022_AMC_10B_Q07#square-discriminant and retains its inherited aops-reference-2022_AMC_10B_Q07 credit. The current AoPS Solution 2 supplies the stated reference basis; the candidate correctly enumerates the smaller factor and supplies the necessary parity justification. No official authorship is claimed.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: Necessity and sufficiency are both explained. The finite factor search explicitly checks all even candidates below 12, including why 10 fails, and handles repeated roots and both signs of k.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_222, cnm_223, cnm_152 and math:integer-diophantine-equations respectively match the quadratic formula, positive discriminant condition, factorization and complete integer search.
